summary: LAG and LEAD read a value from another row, without a self join.
points: LAG(column) reads the previous row, and LEAD(column) reads the next.
Always give them an order: LAG(temp_c) OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY reading_date).
The first row has no previous row, so LAG returns NULL. LAG(x, 1, 0) sets a default.
LAG(x, 2) reads two rows back. The previous row may not be the previous calendar day.

example.explanation: Each reading is compared with the one before it in the same city.
